subject: Cobaltix dedicated sizing: sustained-burst rightsizing & headroom proposal

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltix.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated slab sizing ask — sustained burst profile + SLO targets

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks for taking this — we're progressing toward an org buy and need a concrete dedicated-capacity recommendation for production. High level: we expect a mix of steady sustained traffic with periodic multi-hour bursts during business hours. Goal: avoid cold degradation and hit a p95 latency SLO of 250ms for our recommendation endpoint.

Quick profile:
- Traffic sample attached (cobaltix-prod-qps-sample.csv).
- Average daily token rate: ~350M tokens/day, but more importantly: sustained peak windows of ~14k–20k tokens/sec for 2–4 hour stretches; short-term microbursts up to ~35k tokens/sec for a few minutes.
- Prompt mix: 60% short (~64 tokens), 40% long (~512 tokens), average response length ~48 tokens.
- Candidate models: openlm-70B-quant (we've quantized locally) for best quality; fallback to redwood-13B-q4 for capacity-constrained periods.
- Must support warm KV-cache reuse (many repeated user contexts) — expected cache hit ~65%.

Ask: can you provide tokens/sec to GPU mapping, an SLO fit (p95 latency), and recommended dedicated slab size with headroom assumptions (safety factor). Also include a suggested canary plan (percent of traffic on new slab).

Appreciate a concise sizing sketch by early next week — procurement timeline is tight.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Cobaltix

Subject: Re: Dedicated slab sizing ask — sustained burst profile + SLO targets

Samir — thanks for the context and the sample. Quick read: traffic shape looks like a sustained-daytime ridge with repeat sessions (good for KV reuse). Below is a concise sizing sketch and assumptions; I attached a short workbook (sizing-model-v1.xlsx) with the line-by-line math.

Top-level recommendation (starter): 8x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs in a dedicated slab, split as 6x primary + 2x hot standby/canary. Rationale and assumptions below.

Key assumptions
- Models and per-GPU throughput (tokens/sec) at your mix and target latency (~p95 <= 250ms):
  - openlm-70B-quant (q8/kv-hot path): ~1,200 tokens/sec per A100-like GPU for the long-request mix (512 context); with 65% KV cache hit, effective tokens/sec/projected throughput ~2,600 tokens/sec per GPU when you account for short prompt mix and cache reuse across concurrent sessions.
  - redwood-13B-q4 (fallback): ~7,500 tokens/sec per GPU under same mix and target p95.
- Latency model: p95 dominated by generation time + queueing; we budget 180–210ms generation p95 on 70B when warmed with KV cache, additional 30–40ms network/overhead.
- Safety/headroom: 1.3x on steady peak to cover diurnal variance and degraded KV hit; plus two GPUs reserved as buffer/canary for rolling updates.

Sizing math (summary)
- Target sustained peak to cover: 18,000 tokens/sec (mid-point of your 14–20k).
- If we run primary on openlm-70B-quant: using conservative effective throughput 2,600 tps/GPU -> 18,000 / 2,600 = 6.9 -> round to 7 GPUs.
- Add 1 spare for maintenance/heterogeneous load -> 8 GPUs total.
- Fallback strategy: keep a 13B fleet sized to absorb ~60% of peak if 70B experiences runtime pressure (13B per-GPU ~7,500 tps -> 18,000/7,500 = 2.4 -> 3 GPUs to absorb full peak). We recommend a small 13B pool as warm fallback or cross-route low-priority burst traffic to 13B.

Operational notes
- KV cache reuse: the 65% hit assumption is material — if hits are >75% you can reduce GPUs by ~1; if <50% add +1–2 GPUs.
- Cold starts: plan warmers for new replicas to avoid p95 spikes; include a pre-warm task in rollout.
- Canary: route 5–10% of traffic to the slab initially with autoscaling disabled for the first 48 hours. Use slow roll for model/quant changes.

Estimated SLA fit & cost-risk tradeoffs
- With 8x A100 slab and KV hit ~65% we expect p95 to be inside your 250ms target with ~1.3x steadyheadroom.
- If you want tighter p95 (<=200ms) we should target 10 GPUs or increase cache sizing and prefetching.

I'll attach the workbook with the exact formulas. Ben / Priyom — FYI on follow-up: can you provide a quick put/cost delta for 8x vs 10x slab and a short procurement note we can send Samir?

Next steps
1) We finalize assumptions with Samir (cache hit, exact model variant).
2) We run a small single-GPU microbench with their quantized artifacts (if they can share) to validate tokens/sec.
3) Draft commitment proposal + pricing for 8x slab + optional 2-GPU buffer.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated slab sizing ask — sustained burst profile + SLO targets

Hannah — this is great, thanks. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the sizing: 
1) KV cache: our run-time telemetry suggests effective reuse is 70–75% for recommendation flows (users with sessions and short follow-ups). We can share a sanitized sample of prefix ids if you want to validate.
2) Microburst exposure: the 35k tokens/sec for microbursts comes from sync jobs and a small subset of power users — we can gate and throttle some of that traffic (we'd prefer not to). Would the 8x slab sustain short 35k spikes if we allow queuing/backpressure or would it push p95 beyond 250ms?
3) Cost: can you ballpark monthly committed cost for 8x A100 slab vs 10x? Procurement wants a delta to evaluate plus a 12-month commit discount tier.

Also — we prefer a two-week canary with gradual ramp rather than just 48 hours. Is that compatible with your recommended rollout?

Samir
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobaltix.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated slab sizing ask — sustained burst profile + SLO targets

Samir — good clarifications. Short answers then concrete next steps.

1) KV cache hit of 70–75% improves effective throughput; with 72% hit we'd re-run the sheet and reduce the primary requirement to ~6x GPUs nominal (so 8x with buffer still looks good). Please send the sanitized prefix sample — we'll run a quick cache-modeling pass.

2) Microbursts: 35k short spikes will push p95 above 250ms if fully handled by 8 GPUs without any throttling. Options:
   - Throttle/shed low-priority sync jobs (recommended) so microbursts don't consume headroom; or
   - Temporarily spill excess traffic to a burst pool (13B) — to absorb 35k you'd need ~5 GPUs of 13B (35k/7.5k ~= 4.7) warmed and ready; cheaper but more operational complexity; or
   - Increase dedicated slab to 10x GPUs to reduce p95 risk during spikes.

3) Cost ballpark (committed monthly) — rough numbers to illustrate delta; we'll follow up with formal pricing via contract team: 
   - 8x A100-equivalent slab: $86k/mo (committed tier estimate)
   - 10x A100-equivalent slab: $105k/mo (committed tier estimate)
   - 12-month commit would move you into a deeper discount bracket; I'll have pricing finalize after procurement asks.

4) Canary: two-week ramp is fine. Proposed cadence: 10% week 1, 30% week 2, 60% week 3 then full cutover (you can shorten if telemetry is green). During canary we keep autoscaling disabled and monitor p95, queue depth, and KV hit.

Action items
- Samir: share sanitized prefix sample and confirm whether you can gate/shape sync jobs.
- Ben/Priyom: I'll need the formal 8x vs 10x cost sheet and a one-page procurement note summarizing SLA fit and headroom.
- I'll prepare a tech-runbook for canary and warmers and share the Drive link (shared above).

If that all looks good we'll draft an LOI with a 60-day runway for procurement.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
